Explain the new feature documentation suppressionThe fetched directive reference explicitly describes both arguments; the supplied changed source provides only the diagnostic code. This is a suppression-guidance finding, not a deterministic Documentation Completeness judgment or evidence that VMSS compatibility passed.
Affected intents (1)
Extend shared network properties and update the VMSS dependency
failed

Expected

A #suppress directive supplies the diagnostic code and a message justifying the suppression.

Directives — #suppress
Suppress directive allows suppressing a specific warning diagnostic. It takes 2 arguments: the diagnostic code to suppress, and a message to justify the suppression.
Documented TypeSpec example
#suppress "@typespec/http/no-service-found" "standard library route"

Actual

The newly added firstPartyServiceTag member uses #suppress "@azure-tools/typespec-azure-core/documentation-required" without a justification argument.

Expected

New types introduced for the stable version carry appropriate versioning decoration.

Add stable after stable — Making Changes to your TypeSpec spec
If any types are removed in this stable (unlikely) mark these with an @removed decorator referencing the new version. If any types are added, renamed, or otherwise modified in the new version, mark them with the appropriate versioning decorator.
Evolving APIs — Versioning Decorators
You can add new models, properties, or operations in a specific version and all subsequent versions using the @added decorator. To remove models, properties, or operations starting from a specific version, use the @removed decorator.
Documented TypeSpec example
model Employee {
  name: string;
  @added(Versions.v2)
  city?: string;
}

Actual

The new EnableOnlyIpv6PeeringState union has no @added annotation in its supplied declaration, although the property consuming it is explicitly added in 2025-09-01.

ServiceGateways_UpdateAddressLocationsPOST /subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/resourceGroups/{resourceGroupName}/providers/Microsoft.Network/serviceGateways/{serviceGatewayName}/updateAddressLocations · 2025-09-01
Affected intents (1)
Change service-gateway updates from asynchronous to synchronous
3 changes
Contract areaBeforeAfter
Contract area202
Operation ServiceGateways_UpdateAddressLocations preserves response 202.
Operation ServiceGateways_UpdateAddressLocations no longer defines response 202.
Contract arealro-behavior-changed
Existing long-running HTTP behavior is preserved.
Operation ServiceGateways_UpdateAddressLocations changed long-running HTTP behavior.
Contract area204
Operation ServiceGateways_UpdateAddressLocations preserves response 204.
Operation ServiceGateways_UpdateAddressLocations no longer defines response 204.
Why this is breaking:
  • ServiceGateways_UpdateAddressLocations removes 202 acceptance and its polling headers in favor of 200 JSON. Cross-version callers expecting asynchronous acceptance can no longer use their existing accepted-response and polling path unchanged.
  • ServiceGateways_UpdateAddressLocations changes from 202/204 LRO completion with Location and Retry-After to synchronous 200 JSON without LRO behavior. Migrating clients must consume immediate completion instead of following the old asynchronous protocol.
  • ServiceGateways_UpdateAddressLocations drops the 204 no-content response in 2025-09-01 and documents 200 with a status object. Cross-version response consumers restricted to the prior 204 completion contract require migration.

ServiceGateways_UpdateServicesPOST /subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/resourceGroups/{resourceGroupName}/providers/Microsoft.Network/serviceGateways/{serviceGatewayName}/updateServices · 2025-09-01

3 changes
Contract areaBeforeAfter
Contract area204
Operation ServiceGateways_UpdateServices preserves response 204.
Operation ServiceGateways_UpdateServices no longer defines response 204.
Contract area202
Operation ServiceGateways_UpdateServices preserves response 202.
Operation ServiceGateways_UpdateServices no longer defines response 202.
Contract arealro-behavior-changed
Existing long-running HTTP behavior is preserved.
Operation ServiceGateways_UpdateServices changed long-running HTTP behavior.
Why this is breaking:
  • ServiceGateways_UpdateServices replaces the documented 204 empty completion with 200 JSON in 2025-09-01. Consumers migrating from 2025-07-01 that accept only 204 or assume an empty completion response must change their response handling.
  • ServiceGateways_UpdateServices removes the previous 202 response with Location and Retry-After and returns 200 JSON. Callers migrating versions that require an asynchronous acceptance response can no longer retain their existing polling initiation logic.
  • ServiceGateways_UpdateServices replaces the LRO's 202/204 completion contract with synchronous 200 status JSON. Consumers moving to 2025-09-01 must change asynchronous completion and result consumption, independently of the unchanged route and request.

Extend network feature models and add migration request typesAdd IP-configuration move and NVA migration request types, optional Kubernetes selectors, IPv6/NVA/virtual-hub settings, upgrade indicators, and ExpressRoute resiliency/multicloud options. Unversioned IPv6 helper-type introduction and incomplete model tails require explicit qualifications.

+/**
+ * The type of diagnostic operation to run on a connection analyzer.
+ */
+@added(Versions.v2025_09_01)
+union DiagnosticOperation {
+  string,
+
+  /**
+   * Determines the next hop for traffic from the source to the destination.
+   */
+  NextHop: "NextHop",
+
+  /**
+   * Evaluates the network security group rules that apply to the traffic.
+   */
+  NSG: "NSG",
+
+  /**
+   * Scans the destination ports to determine their reachability.
+   */
+  PortScan: "PortScan",
+
+  /**
+   * Performs an end-to-end connectivity check between the source and destination.
+   */
+  ConnectivityCheck: "ConnectivityCheck",
+
+  /**
+   * Runs Express Route specific diagnostics for the connection.
+   */
+  ExpressRouteDiagnostic: "ExpressRouteDiagnostic",
+}
+
+namespace ConnectionAnalyzerEndpointTypes {
+  /**
+   * The endpoint type for a connection analyzer source or destination.
+   */
+  @added(Versions.v2025_09_01)
+  union EndpointType {
+    string,
+
+    /**
+     * An Azure virtual machine endpoint, identified by its ARM resource ID.
+     */
+    VM: "VM",
+
+    /**
+     * An Azure virtual machine scale set (or scale set instance) endpoint, identified by its ARM resource ID.
+     */
+    VMSS: "VMSS",
+
+    /**
+     * An external endpoint reachable from outside Azure, identified by an IP address or FQDN.
+     */
+    ExternalAddress: "ExternalAddress",
+
+    /**
+     * An Azure Bastion host endpoint, identified by its ARM resource ID.
+     */
+    BastionHost: "BastionHost",
+
+    /**
+     * An Application Gateway endpoint, identified by its ARM resource ID.
+     */
+    ApplicationGateway: "ApplicationGateway",
+  }
+}
+
+/**
+ * Current execution status of the connection analyzer.
+ */
+@added(Versions.v2025_09_01)
+union ConnectionAnalyzerStatus {
+  string,
+
+  /**
+   * The connection analyzer has been created but execution has not yet begun.
+   */
+  NotStarted: "NotStarted",
+
+  /**
+   * The connection analyzer is currently running its diagnostic operations.
+   */
+  Running: "Running",
+
+  /**
+   * The connection analyzer completed all diagnostic operations successfully.
+   */
+  Succeeded: "Succeeded",
+
+  /**
+   * The connection analyzer failed to complete its diagnostic operations.
+   */
+  Failed: "Failed",
+}

+  resourceId?: armResourceIdentifier;
